text: Every lesson so far has happened inside Power BI Desktop. Starting now, the other half of Power BI — the service — takes over.
Desktop is where you connect to data, clean it, model it, and write DAX. It's local authoring software. Publishing sends your work somewhere else entirely.

That somewhere else is the Power BI service — a website, not a program you install. It's where finished work gets stored, refreshed on a schedule, and shared with people who never open Desktop at all.

Five concepts run through this entire chapter: the workspace that holds everything, the semantic model your reports are built from, the report itself, dashboards that pin tiles from reports, and apps that package it all for a broad audience.
You can't create a workspace inside Desktop — that only happens in the service. Lesson 68 starts with what license you actually need to do any of this.
